reason: The single cited study (E1) directly supports all key premises: it shows Hf-rich phase precipitation at interfaces, hindrance of grain boundary sliding and dislocation movement, improved high-temperature strength and ductility at low Hf contents, and nearly unchanged room-temperature performance. However, the premise about density is not explicitly addressed in the cited passage, representing a minor gap.
premises: Hf addition induces precipitation of Hf-rich interfacial phases in dual-phase refractory HEAs
These precipitates impede dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding at high temperature
High-temperature strength and ductility improve with small Hf additions
Room-temperature mechanical properties remain almost unchanged with Hf addition
Density is not significantly increased by small Hf additions
